# New constructive-mechanism comparison, 13 November 2026
Selected question: which concrete unpaid operation can now close an end-to-end algorithm or decisively match it classically? Two independent directions, selected after STATE/TRAPS, corpus lookup and primary literature. This is not a retry of empty prior requests: the sparse task targets structured Sylvester determinants/small cyclotomic places, the Gaudin task targets an explicit generator equation rather than a gap or prefix formula.

1. SPARSE RELATIONS: native Q(T_1,...,T_s)[Y]/monic irreducible f, degree delta charged numerically, all coefficients explicit sparse rational functions with binary T exponents; growing s,delta,k. Nonzero original u_i are explicit in the Y basis. Full Rel={e in Z^k:product u_i^e=1}. Written bounded-error quantum polynomial sparse-bit endpoint exists through large-prime full-algebra finite HSP. General Alg={e:product u_i^e algebraic over Q} already has a proved classical polynomial sparse-bit algorithm. Do not redo Alg. Missing classical step: complete constant relations without huge powers, expanded huge-height rational specializations or hidden aligned embeddings. Degrees1/2 and monomial Kummer are classically matched. Expected upside here is decisive dequantization of the FULL endpoint, not an extra quantum primitive. Strongest baselines and falsifiers are in supplied notes.

2. GAUDIN: N spin1/2 qubits, distinct rational eps_i, coupling g from0 toG, input bitstring b fixes branch atg0. Q_i(g)=n_i+(g/2)sum_(j!=i)(P_ij-I)/(eps_i-eps_j). All charges explicit and commuting, preserve M=sum n_i. Want target instantaneous joint eigenstate traced from b, TD<=epsilon, poly(N,nativebits,1/epsilon) with G and inverse spacing charged polynomial. No roots/eigenvalues/eigenvectors or schedule advice. Current joint-dephasing path is conditional on inverse-polynomial same-sector gap; uniform1/N squared gap is disproved but weaker polynomial gap unknown. New mechanism: explicit polynomially describable anti-Hermitian real generator K(g), with [Q_j,Q_i' - [K,Q_i]]=0 for all i,j; physical AGP A=iK. Polynomial integral norm/derivative/control cost would pay branch preparation without using spectral denominators. Exact K=whole Hilbert-space linear solution is exponentially large, not an algorithm. Classical counterparts: root continuation under actual conditioning, MPS under paid bond bounds, ALL-prefix norm sampling (currently unpaid), and exact small-sector linear algebra falsifiers.

All reports advisory. Separate deductions, conditional algorithms, finite falsifiers, source imports and speculation. Give exact quantifiers, access, asymptotic costs and an explicit cheapest disproof. No hardness/novelty/speedup from failure. No tools/browsing are provided. Cite source hypotheses precisely, mark any unavailable external theorem unverified. Prefer a usable concise final result over exhausting all thinking tokens without a response.

# New parent proposal: torus logarithms plus vertical valuations

Full native growing-delta sparse relation contract is unchanged. GeneralAlg is already classically computed. This is a different operation from leading-place or cyclotomic specialization: approximate ARCHIMEDEAN logarithms at a random complex torus point, then combine with finite vertical valuations. Neither piece alone is an algorithm.

Parent elementary analytic proposal to attack: for a NONZERO INTEGER multivariate polynomial H with l1norm<=A, iterated Jensen gives m(H)=E_theta log|H(exp(i theta))|>=0. Since log^+|H|<=log A, E log^-|H|<=log A. Thus P(|H|<exp(-t))<=logA/t. Native denominator/norm/discriminant polynomials can be implicit: determinant l1norm bounds have logA polynomial in sparse input bits, although degrees are exponential. Taking t polynomial gives constant-probability simultaneous nonvanishing/conditioning. A dyadic phase grid with resolution paying degree*norm Lipschitz bound needs only polynomially many BITS (logdegree enters). Verify both the argument and complete finite-precision cost, including ALL delta root branches, cancellations, logarithms and correct conjugate embedding grouping of the constant field. Repeated constant-success trials may cost log1/eta; do not use a 1/eta precision as if logarithmic.

If this works, every original u_i has moderate logarithmic absolute values in each complex branch and can be evaluated to polynomially many bits. Multiply these logarithm rows by the known Alg-basis integer matrix without expanding algebraic products. The retained elementary height gap for degree<=delta non-torsion constants is exp(-poly(delta)); with ALL places, this could pay a logarithmic-lattice relation algorithm. Archimedean rows alone FAIL: (3+4i)/5 is not a root of unity but every archimedean absolute value is1. No arch-only relation claim.

Concrete finite-place obligation: construct polynomially many vertical Gauss-valuation rows on the ORIGINAL u_i, retaining their joint constant-field embeddings, so on Alg their kernel gives algebraic UNITS. For integral monic f and integral u_i, every possible finite-prime contribution lies over primes dividing CONTENT_T Norm(u_i), since nonnegative branch valuations and primitive norm imply all are zero. For rational coefficient polynomials include all relevant denominator contents/norms and field lattice denominators. These implicit resultant contents have polynomial BIT size but computing a nonzero coefficient/content is NOT automatically paid by PIT. Factoring polynomial-bit explicit integers is allowed as a separately charged resource if necessary; no factorization of enormous expanded evaluations, hidden constant-field basis, sparse determinant leading coefficient oracle, or extra advice.

Potential approach: modular specialization in an unramified p-adic extension of degree O(logdegree) avoids nonzero residual polynomials with a polynomial-bit representation; Newton polygons/lifting in Y have charged degree delta. The hard point is FINDING the complete finite prime support and aligned valuations, not merely evaluating at supplied primes. Construct that operation or give a native obstruction to this precise claim. If complete arch+finite rows are available, exact constants of zero height are torsion, with order bounded in degree delta, but exact identity still needs a paid root-of-unity phase step. Every claim must preserve all growing parameters. No algorithm/speedup inferred from these sketches.

Prior check: fresh corpus queries found existing height-gap and differentialAlg arguments, not this torus+vertical compiler. Literature search supplied only general Mahler/Ge leads; no additional theorem is admitted without actual source. Retained LS finiteQalgebra theorem cannot be applied to implicit giant constants. This proposal is supplied for falsification/derivation, not as an established result.


FILE: research/GENERAL_SPARSE_CONSTANTS_ATTACK.md
# General sparse function-field constants: classical attack

7 November2026. Reviewed pass complete. General Alg recovery is established;
the FULL classical Rel counterpart remains open. No new constant-map
subsystem or nearby refinement is queued. Full native question: can a classical
polynomial sparse-BIT algorithm replace the quantum relation step for EVERY
F=Q(T_1,...,T_s)[Y]/f with monic irreducible f of charged degree delta,
nonzero u_i in Y basis, sparse rational coefficients and binary T exponents?
Return FULL Rel={e:u^e=1}; s,delta,k grow, error<=eta. No place, constant
field, inverse or relation advice. Native contract and the reviewed quantum
upper bound are in SPARSE_CHARZERO_FUNCTION_FIELD_RELATIONS.md.

## Selection, mechanism and falsifiers

Fresh STATE/TRAPS, corpus been-tried and baselines preceded selection.
Independent directions were compared: inverse-trace search is already
classically matched on its native odd-degree sequence; bare supersingular
walk amplification leaves a square-root success cost; bilinear tensor-graph
Fourier outcomes have an exact classical Gaussian-elimination sampler.
No new end-to-end operation emerged there. The present attack instead tries
to remove the quantum step from an existing FULL native algorithm. It is
not a new restricted easy-face promise or a new quantum primitive.

Mechanism: compute Alg={e:u^e algebraic overQ} by all extended logarithmic
derivatives; compute a multiplicative leading-coefficient map to a small
number field, injective on constants, retaining ORIGINAL small atoms and
binary exponents; apply existing classical Lenstra--Silverberg relations
and integer intersection. Expected result if ALL gates close: polynomial
classical sparse-BIT fullRel, matching the known polynomial quantum upper
bound. The full constant-map gate is currently UNPAID. No speedup, novelty,
full classical solver or quantum execution claim.

Baseline: existing delta1/2 and monomialKummer classical algorithms;
finite-Q-algebra LS1509.08843 Thm1.11; numerical-degree valuation/factorization
algorithms. Dense factorization, giant characteristic-zero evaluation,
unstated sparse Puiseux clocks, or noncommutative determinant results after
commutative specialization are not valid substitutes. Actual Oki ICALP2020
Remark12 distinguishes numerical-degree clocks from sparse determinant-degree:
https://drops.dagstuhl.de/opus/volltexte/2020/12496/pdf/LIPIcs-ICALP-2020-89.pdf.
This source does not prove hardness of our map or exclude randomized algorithms.

## 1. Independently reviewed general-Alg algorithm

Clear rational scalar coefficients within each numerator/denominator pair.
Let D=product of ALL coefficient denominator polynomials, L their number,
b>=1 satisfy product_P max(2,||P||_1)<=2^b over input numerators/denominators,
H=2^b, and beta>=1 bound totalT degree. Put d0=(L+1)beta. Every coefficient
of f or u_i can be written p/D with ||p||_1,||D||_1<=H and degree<=d0.
These expressions are formal bounds, not expanded products. Zero numerators
are permitted. No cancellation of huge sparse exponents is required.

For multiplication byY let C=A/D be the delta-dimensional companion matrix.
Every entry of A has norm<=H and degree<=d0. The following matrices have
explicit formal numerator presentations with the indicated common powers:
    M(u_i)=A_i/D^delta,
    M(f_Y)=J/D^(delta-1),
    M((u_i)_Tj)=T_ji/D^(delta+1),
    M(f_Tj)=F_j/D^(delta+1),
    M((u_i)_Y)=Y_i/D^(delta-1).
Here T derivatives keep Y FORMALLY FIXED; later extend by
partial_j Y= -f_Tj/f_Y. The numerators use sums of powers of A, denominator
powers and ordinary numerator derivatives. Set
    U=[2(delta+1)(d0+1)H]^(2delta+4), e0=(delta+1)d0,
    V=delta! U^delta.
Every displayed numerator entry has l1norm<=U and degree<=e0: rational
coefficient derivatives have numerator p'D-pD', norm<=2d0H², and powers
of A contribute at most delta^(h-1)H^h per entry. Determinants and adjugate
entries have norm<=V. All logarithms of these bounds are polynomial in
native inputbits, including log(beta); none is a numerical-degree runtime.

Since char0 and f irreducible, f_Y is nonzero and invertible. Each u_i is
nonzero and invertible. After combining the extended derivative and u_i^-1,
    dlog_j u_i = [T_ji detJ - Y_i adjJ F_j] adjA_i
                / [D detJ detA_i],
as multiplication matrices applied to the vector1. A common denominator is
    h=D detJ product_i detA_i.
Multiply the numerator for i by product_(l!=i)detA_l. Every integer
coefficient of every resulting basis-coordinate polynomial is bounded by
    C0=2(delta+1)^3 U² V^(k+1),
and its totaldegree is at most (k+1)delta e0. The denominator h is nonzero,
has norm<=C0 and degree<=Dstar=d0+(k+1)delta e0. These are polynomial-BIT
bounds on an implicit matrix with k columns; its potentially huge number
of coefficient rows is never constructed.

In characteristic0 the common kernel of all s extended derivations is
exactly the algebraic constants. Hence the integer kernel of this implicit
coefficient matrix is Alg, a SATURATED lattice. The standard minor/HNF
kernel estimate gives a basis bound <=k!C0^k; conservatively use
    Balg=(2kC0)^(2k), R=2^k k Balg.
Choose a random prime p in[X,2X], where X exceeds 2kR C0 and
16(1+(2R+1)^k)Dstar/eta, and use capped prime generation as in the priornote.
All nonzero bounded-exponent numerator coefficients survive reduction;
h survives too. For uniform t in F_p^s, union-bound Schwartz--Zippel over h
and ONE nonzero coordinate polynomial for EACH false exponent in[-R,R]^k
bounds the bad point probability by eta/8. Exponent-box enumeration is
PROOF-ONLY. Reject bad denominators, nonunit f_Y and u_i.

Evaluate the logarithmic derivative matrix in the FULL finite algebra
F_p[Y]/f_t, retaining every Y-basis coefficient and every partial derivative.
It may be reducible; the f_Y unit test forces f_t to be squarefree.
No factorization is required.
Finite-field linear algebra computes its complete integer CONGRUENCE kernel
M (full rankk). On the good event Alg is contained in M and every vector
of M with infinitynorm<=R lies in Alg. Apply exact3/4-LLL in Z^k.

For rankr=rank Alg, lambda_r(M)<=sqrt(k)Balg, so the first r LLL vectors
have norm<=2^((k-1)/2)sqrt(k)Balg<R and belong to Alg. They span its real
space. Every later LLL vector lies outside that space and therefore has
infinitynorm>R. LLL size/Lovasz bounds give ||b_j||<=2^((k-1)/2)||b_j*||,
so all later Gram--Schmidt lengths exceed sqrt(k)Balg. Expanding any of the
short TRUE Alg basis vectors in the full M basis, its largest nonzero index
cannot be later thanr. Thus the first r vectors generate the WHOLE Alg,
not a finite-index sublattice. Select the prefix of norm<=R. Rank0/fullrank
are included. This gives a randomized polynomial sparse-BIT algorithm for
Alg only; algebraic constants and roots of unity are not thereby removed.

## 2. Independently reviewed direct-specialization falsifier

Let delta>=5 and even binary M>=2. Put
    A=2+T^M, B=T^M(T^M-1)A,
    f(T,Y)=product_(j=1)^delta(Y-jA)-B,
    u_j=Y-jA.
This is a promised native family with O(delta²) sparse monomials after
expanding the Y coefficients and polynomial coefficient BITlength.
A is irreducible by Eisenstein at2. Every nonleading Y coefficient of f
is divisible by A, and its constant coefficient divided by A is congruent
to -6 modulo A, because B/A is6 modulo A. Thus f is Eisenstein at prime
polynomial A, hence irreducible in Q(T)[Y]. All u_j are nonzero.

AtT=0, the delta branches have distinct constant terms2j. On branchj the
unit u_j cancels this first term and begins at orderM with coefficient
    -2^(2-delta)/product_(l!=j)(j-l).
At infinity the branches have distinct leading terms jT^M, but unit u_j
on branchj first has exponent M(4-delta); the relative cancellation depth
is M(delta-3). Therefore picking a simple branch does not make every
original unit's naive LC nonzero, and ordinary truncation through numerical
order costs exponentially in logM. Norm(u_j)=+/-B repairs this displayed cancellation by combining the known
other-branch leading coefficients. It does NOT identify constants alone:
u_i/u_j has norm1 and is nonconstant. At branchj overT=0, only u_j has
valuationM; all other u_i have valuation0. These valuations show Alg=0 for
THIS tuple, so its full relation problem is actually easy. The obstruction
is to the proposed operation, not the native problem. No general Puiseux
or norm-repair impossibility follows.

More strongly, for EVERY rational specialization a where all u_j can remain
units, expanded monic f_a has exponential coefficient height. At a=0,1,-1,
B(a)=0, f_a splits as product(Y-jA(a)), and localizing ALL u_j yields the
zero algebra. Those are not permissible good points. Every other rational a
has h(a)>=log2. Standard rational height inequalities give
    h(A(a))>=M h(a)-log4.
The coefficient of Y^(delta-1) is -delta(delta+1)A(a)/2, so its height is
at least M log2-log4-log(delta(delta+1)/2). Writing that supplied monic
presentation costs Omega(M) bits (take fixed delta or M much larger than
logdelta). This refutes a direct rational-specialization/poly-expanded-height
shortcut. It does NOT exclude changing primitive element/presentation,
compact atoms, nonrational specialization, or a different full algorithm.

## 3. Remaining gate and closed admission decision

The single scientific question remains the FULL classical counterpart.
GeneralAlg is an intermediate lemma that removes a specific first blocker;
it is not the requested full result. A paid constant map or alternative
constant-relation operation must still work uniformly in growingdelta,
all sparse inputs and binary exponents. No easy-face subclass is substituted.

Another precise shortcut fails even in the already classically solved quadratic
case. In F=Q(T)[Y]/(Y²-2T²), c=3+2Y/T and c^-1=3-2Y/T have identical
individual norm1, trace6 and characteristic polynomial X²-6X+1. The tuples
(c,c) and(c,c^-1) both have Alg=Z², but their Rel lattices are respectively
Z(1,-1) and Z(1,1), since c>1 in a real embedding. Individual characteristic
polynomials therefore lose joint embedding alignment. Mixed traces can
separate this pair; no lower bound against joint algebra methods follows.
This counterexample was independently proposed and checked directly here.

A small cyclotomic specialization would finish the constants step IF its
degree and good-point search were paid; no such general operation was found.
Do not apply sparse support-count bounds to the potentially exponential
expanded support of an implicit norm/determinant. The current attack does
not prove that a classical constant operation is impossible. It does not
replace the full question by a generic easy-initial-face promise. Reopen
with a concrete operation that handles the complete native model; otherwise
compare independent directions, rather than adding more nearby barriers.

## 4. Review, exact control and terminal API outcomes

Core review: audits/reviews/2026-11-07-general-sparse-constants-core.md.
It checks all five denominator exponents, the extended derivative formula,
U/V/C0/Dstar bounds, nonzero reduction, full congruence kernel and FULL LLL
prefix, including rank0/fullrank. Its norm-scope clarification is incorporated
above: the counterfamily's displayed tuple actually has Alg=0.

One exact CLASSICAL CAS control is
    audits/controls/general_sparse_constants/control.py
and its JSON. In the original quartic basis for (Y²-T^N)²-2, N=2^40+1,
it retains all four coefficients, uses only binary modular powering, and
recovers Alg rank5 for seven original units. The finite-algebra derivative
matrix has rank2; its full integer congruence lattice has index p². Exact
LLL returns the expected integral lattice, with no finite-index loss and
later Gram--Schmidt lengths beyond the short true basis. This case has
constants Q(sqrt2); sqrt2 is not1, and -1 has order2. Three explicit true
relations verify the constant/torsion distinction. No generic LS or fullRel
algorithm was executed. Control-only Balg=1 is NOT the theorem-sized bound.

At p257 dividing N, the derivative rank drops to1 and falsely admits Y,
confirming the essential characteristic requirement. A symbolic X=T^M
counterfamily control checks Eisenstein residue-6, all f(jA)=-B and the
coefficient causing specialization growth, without expanding M. First run
stopped on Sage gram_schmidt returning two objects rather than three; fixing
that API unpacking let the complete control pass. No formula was weakened.
The control proves no all-input theorem, confidence bound or growing-degree
runtime; those are in the reviewed derivation.

Primary source Oki's actual Remark12 is retained under
    audits/sources/general_sparse_constants/oki.pdf/.txt/source.json.
Earlier LS, kernel/LLL and prime-density source contracts are reused from
the preceding sparse-function-field notes; no source scope is expanded.

Claude input packets under audits/claude_inputs/2026-11-07-general-sparse-constants/
and runner bundles under audits/claude_runs/2026-11-07-general-sparse-
{derivative,constant-map} retain exact snapshots. Both calls are TERMINAL
with EMPTY response files. Opus derivative: refusal,10515 input/8102 output,
estimated USD0.2041. Opus constant-map: max_tokens,10382 input/32768 output,
estimated USD0.696888. Total USD0.900988. No report, accepted finding, retry,
pending call or exact balance inference. All mathematical claims above were
derived and independently checked outside these empty calls.

Disposition: general Alg is a complete WRITTEN classical polynomial sparse-BIT
algorithm; only the narrow control was executed. Full native classical Rel
remains OPEN at the compact constants operation. No full classical solver,
novelty, separation, quantum execution or general map-impossibility claim.

Milestone checks passed: STATE/title/Now/boundary row, actual Oki PDF hash,
both immutable API request/context bundles and terminal usage, core review,
exact control values/false gates, and scoped diff/whitespace. No full suite,
unrelated rerun, Git commit or balance inference.


FILE: research/SPARSE_CHARZERO_FUNCTION_FIELD_RELATIONS.md
# Sparse characteristic-zero function-field relations

2026-11-06. WRITTEN bounded-error quantum polynomial-bit composition, with
independent core/source/resource and actual-text reviews complete. Full
classical sparse-bit counterparts for degrees1 and2 are also reviewed.
No novelty, separation or full algorithm execution claim.

## Native question and independent selection

Input: F=Q(T_1,...,T_s)[Y]/f, with f monic irreducible of charged numerical
degree delta>=1, and k>=1 nonzero elements u_i in its Y-power basis. Every
rational-function coefficient is an explicit quotient of sparse polynomials
with binary rational coefficients and BINARY T exponents. s,delta,k all grow;
unused variables are dropped. Irreducibility and nonzeroness are promises.
No inverses, factorization, constants, valuations, points or relations are
supplied. Output the full lattice Rel={e in Z^k:u^e=1}, with error<=eta,
in time polynomial in the sparse input BIT length and log1/eta.

Question: does random large-prime specialization preserve all short false-
relation witnesses well enough for a paid finite-ring relation algorithm and
LLL to recover the exact lattice, including algebraic constant units?
Unlike characteristic p, constants need not be torsion. Bounds on their
relation basis and on bad primes must be proved, not supplied as advice.

Selection followed current STATE/TRAPS, corpus been-tried then literature,
and corpus baselines (which returned no precise sparse-relation entry).
Independent alternatives were checked first. Actual Kedlaya0411623v3
Theorem1 and Sections6--8 already supply growing-genus curve zeta via
canonical Jacobian groups; no new operation was identified there. Actual
Ding--Zhan--Preskill--Lin2508.05703v3 Theorems1--3 give mixing promises for
free systems and high-temperature local commuting systems, not the missing
low-temperature lattice transfer. The syndrome-driver alternative repeats
the scoped sqrt(overlap) two-projector gap in NATIVE_SYNDROME_DILATION.md;
no general annealing no-go follows. Growing-degree Legendre reconstruction
still lacks a paid replacement for its factorial split-mask cost. None
justified building a new subsystem. This explicit symbolic-algebra problem
has an end-to-end candidate and a decisive classical attack, so it won this
pass's comparison; it is not selected merely as an arithmetic continuation.

Classical comparators: Lenstra--Silverberg1509.08843 Thm1.11 for explicit
finite Q-algebras (s=0); the earlier fixed-variable/numerical-degree affine
composition; Kreuzer--Walsh2307.09394 valuation algorithms; and Giesbrecht--
Roche0901.1848v2 lacunary perfect-power tests under their actual scope.
Dense factorization or expansion is not polynomial in binary sparse degrees.
Section4 gives a full classical sparse-bit algorithm for delta=1. No
classical lower bound is asserted for delta>1. The quantum candidate reduces
to standard finite abelian HSP/DLog and is not a new quantum primitive.

## 1. Uniform bound including algebraic constant relations

First clear rational scalar coefficients with a COMMON multiplier for each
numerator/denominator polynomial pair, preserving their ratio and retaining
integer polynomials. Let beta>=1 bound numerical total T degree,
L count coefficient denominators, and b>=1 satisfy
prod_P max(2,||P||_1)<=2^b, with occurrences retained. These are computable
bounds of polynomial binary length. Set
m=s+1+L+k, D=max(2,beta+delta+2), B0=k!*D^((m+1)*k).
The proof-only affine domain obtained by adjoining denominator inverses and
unit inverses has these variable/degree bounds. Actual2610.27250v1 Prop3.1
proof gives an Alg basis with infinity norm<=B0, where
Alg={e:u^e algebraic over Q}. Its uniform size proof, not its fixed-parameter
enumeration clock, is used. No presentation or basis power is expanded.

A proof-only finite specialization bounds heights of the constants. Use
Hdeg=L*beta, J=delta^2*(Hdeg+beta), W=Hdeg+k*J. The polynomial formed by
input denominators and generic multiplication-matrix determinants is nonzero
and has degree<=W. Hence some integer t in{0,...,W}^s avoids it. Specialize
to the full nonzero degree-delta Q-algebra and choose ANY residue number
field E, of degree<=delta. Let C_A be the algebraic-over-Q elements in the localized affine domain A.
It is a FIELD: the inverse of any nonzero algebraic element is a polynomial
in that element. It contains every Alg-basis product and maps injectively
into E. The entire constant field of Frac(A) need not be contained in A
(e.g. sqrt2=Y/T in Q[T,Y]/(Y²-2T²)); no such containment is assumed. The point and E are PROOF
objects only, not inputs or computed by the algorithm.

Let Hc=b+beta*ceil(log2(W+1))+1 and H=(delta+1)^4*(Hc+1).
Evaluated coefficient numerators/denominators have bit height<=Hc.
Clearing the at most delta rational coefficients of f_t bounds a root's
logarithmic Weil height by (delta+1)Hc+delta. The elementary height sum and
product inequalities then bound h(u_i(t))<=H in E. Therefore the r<=k
constant products c_j arising from an Alg basis satisfy h(c_j)<=k*B0*H.
Both H and this bound can be huge numerically, but their BINARY lengths
are polynomial. No actual value or expanded product is constructed.

Here is a self-contained sufficient lower height bound. Put
Tdelta=2^(delta+2), Kdelta=delta*(2*Tdelta+1)^(delta+1)+1,
epsilon0=1/(delta*Kdelta).
Every algebraic number of degree<=delta and height<=1/delta has a primitive
integer minimal polynomial whose coefficients have absolute value<Tdelta,
by the Mahler-measure/coefficient bound. There are fewer than Kdelta such
numbers, counting all roots of all padded degree<=delta polynomials. If a
nonzero alpha had h(alpha)<epsilon0, its first Kdelta powers would all lie
in that finite set; two would coincide, forcing alpha to be a root of unity.
Thus every non-torsion element of E has height>=epsilon0. No analytic
unproved assumption or computed constant field is used.

Embed the subgroup generated by the c_j modulo roots of unity into weighted
logs at ALL relevant finite AND archimedean places of E. Its l1 norm is
exactly2h, not merely the archimedean norm. Northcott finiteness implies this
finitely generated image is a discrete lattice. Its real rank is<=k;
nonzero vectors have norm>=epsilon0 and generators norm<=G=2*k*B0*H.
An outer John ellipsoid gives a Euclidean norm between l1/sqrt(k) and l1.
For an abstract3/4-LLL basis of this lattice, Gram--Schmidt lengths are
>=2^(-(k-1)/2)*epsilon0/sqrt(k). Back substitution using |mu_ij|<=1/2
bounds the INTEGER coordinates of every original generator by
M=ceil(2^(3k)*k*G/epsilon0).
The ellipsoid, log lattice and basis are only existence arguments. If the
real rank is0, skip them and use the whole exponent lattice as the coordinate
kernel; the same final bound remains valid.

The integer coordinate matrix therefore has kernel basis bounded by k!*M^k
(the determinant/HNF kernel argument from Prop3.1). This is the lattice of
constant products that are roots of unity. Its exact-relation sublattice has
index at most |mu(E)|<=2*delta^2: phi(w)<=delta and phi(w)^2>=w/2. HNF
and lifting through the Alg basis give a FULL Rel basis bounded by

                   B=2*k^2*delta^2*B0*k!*M^k.                  (1)

This retains nonsaturation. logB is polynomial in the original sparse input.
Independent Codex core and complete algorithm/source/resource reviews
accept this bound and its use. No geometric or logarithmic object above is advice.

## 2. Content and degree bounds for random prime specialization

Set R=2^k*k*B, Fbox=(2R+1)^k, Cdeg=(k+2)*J. Use the formal product Gden
of coefficient denominators. As in the characteristic-p note, multiplication
M_i=A_i/Gden^delta has polynomial matrix numerator degree
